reason: The default remains logically readable, but oversized yes/no diamonds and narrow multi-line evidence ellipses turn a compact diagonal chart into a long portrait. It requires far more scanning than the original.
dsl_nastiness: Moderate. Eleven sizes, eleven pins and explicit ports on all twelve edges are required to recover the stair. Three complete custom swatches are verbose for a small palette. The source is readable, but a diagram that is visually simple has accumulated substantial geometry.
residuals: Four text-overflow warnings on final 52-pixel yes/no diamonds; visible words remain inside the outlines.
Native diamonds are square, whereas source yes/no marks are flatter.
No inline weight/color emphasis or panel double outlines.
Manual placement and fixed heights reduce resilience to longer labels.
observed: Original, v0, v1 and v2 images visually inspected; final native CLI checks, geometry, SVG and PNG were executed.
predicted: Label-edit resilience is an unexecuted assessment; no edit-resilience experiment or pixel-error registration was performed.
